audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer rows 0, 3, 4 and 5 all read 'Skill'; the content layer and the packet levelChart both give Ziggs level 1 and levels 4-5, and Orianna level 6 and first item.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 against her 815 ball, so the early poke war is his; from 6 she has a 410-range Shockwave against the least mobile mid in the game, whose only escape is a 20s Satchel Charge.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved onto the content/packet verdict on those four rows with whys and ratings rewritten. Row 6 already agreed and was left alone. win[] already held the correct tokens.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase whys were generic Orianna boilerplate that never named a Ziggs spike.
audit.why: His spike is levels 4-5 with Bouncing Bomb, Satchel and the 16s Hexplosive Minefield zoning the wave; hers is level 6, because Shockwave plus a jungler kills an immobile mage.
audit.corrected: Whys now key to those ranges and cooldowns on their own rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: No interaction stated, and the Short Fuse auto-reset was never mentioned.
audit.why: Short Fuse periodically empowers his next basic attack and every ability cast shortens that timer, so the wind-up on the empowered auto is the tell that his trade has begun. Satchel Charge knocks him away as well as you — it is both his escape and his disengage, and while it is down he cannot leave. Both his Q and his R are projectiles, as is your Q.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d now states the auto-reset tell; the cooldowns field carries Satchel 20s->12s, the minefield's flat 16s and the 120s ult.

audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge 20/18/16/14/12, Hexplosive Minefield 16s, Mega Inferno Bomb 120s at 5000 range stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, and dontsFull[0].d called a single male enemy 'they'.
audit.why: Lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED plus a pronoun defect.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten against his own numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.mid claimed protect-ball 'doubles every gank' (lint UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE).
audit.corrected: Replaced with what the ball actually delivers.

edits.before: Ball on the wave, autos on his face — your passive-stacked autos win level 1 against almost every mid. Place, don't throw.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 against your 815 ball, so he pokes you off the wave and level 1 has no safe answer.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-W every wave contact now. The Dissonance field controls every step he takes near the ball.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb, Satchel and a 16s minefield zone you off the wave — farm the back edge, take only safe CS.

edits.before: Shockwave online — your lane presence doubles without casting anything. Every wave he contests is a potential flip.
edits.after: Shockwave online against the least mobile mid in the game — his only escape is a 20s Satchel self-knockback.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-W chunks a third of his bar. Shove, rotate, and let the ball-delivery threat run the river fights.
edits.after: Luden's and you roam: he cannot follow, so shove the wave, leave, and all-in whenever his Satchel is spent.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Command: Protect like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge (W): 20s at rank 1 and 12s at rank 5 — his only escape, so he is catchable every second it is down. - Hexplosive Minefield (E): a flat 16s — walk around the mines rather than through the slow. - Mega Inferno Bomb: 120s at rank 1, thrown from 5000.

edits.before: From Luden's you run rivers: shove the wave, hover the ball at the choke, and Shockwave the first clump that contests. Protect-ball on your jungler doubles every gank.
edits.after: From Luden's you run rivers: shove, hover the ball at the choke, and Shockwave the immobile back line. Protect-ball brings a shield, the speed field and your R to the gank.

edits.before: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: His Q bounces 850 — park the ball where he must stand to farm and make that range cost him.

edits.before: Ball on his farm path, Q-W the last-hit contact, auto-weave once, and recall the ball — three-second trades his combo math can't answer.
edits.after: Your Q is 7s at rank 1 falling to 3s against his 6s Bouncing Bomb, so take the contact whenever his bomb has just bounced.

edits.before: Ziggs spends Satchel Charge early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Short Fuse resets his auto — the wind-up is the tell, so step back on that, not on the cast.

edits.before: That’s Ziggs’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Ball-less, his 850 Q out-ranges you and he never has to step up.

edits.before: Poking with the ball stranded at max range when his engage is up — an Orianna without her ball is a Doran's Ring with legs.
edits.after: Your R is 110s at rank 1 and it is the one tool that kills an immobile poke mage — never spend it on a wave.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by out-ranging you at 850, mining the ground you farm on, and Satchelling away the moment you step up.

edits.before: If Ziggs takes first blood, tighten up: Satchel Charge is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q-W clears and stay relevant through Shockwave threat.
edits.after: A kill funds his poke items and the 850-range chip becomes unaffordable, so farm the back edge and stop contesting his range. Two kills: play for the level-6 collapse with your jungler, since he still cannot leave without Satchel.

edits.before: Carry through the ball — no champion controls teamfight space like Orianna; one Shockwave on three is a won game, and you decide when it happens.
edits.after: Carry through the ball — he has no dash at all, so one flank Shockwave onto his back line ends the fight before his poke ever matters.

notes: Four full-layer chart rows disagreed with the content layer and the packet (rows 0, 3, 4, 5); the full layer was moved onto their shared verdict and win[] needed no edit. The content layer for this matchup was already specific and largely correct, so the work was on the full layer. Short Fuse's auto-reset tell from missingInteractions is now stated. I did NOT act on the other missing-interaction headline: the kit flags Satchel Charge as percentHealth ('bypasses stacking resistances'), but Riot's own description of Satchel Charge is a flat magic-damage explosion with a knockback and says nothing about percent health or resistance bypass. Per the rule that the description wins over a misfiring derived flag, I left that claim out rather than telling a reader armour and MR are the wrong buy on evidence I do not have. | COHERENCE: 1 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
